title: SpireBench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Strategic Play of Agentic Models with Slay the Spire
abstract: arXiv:2610.12596v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agentic large language models now tackle complex tasks, yet strategic reasoning over long horizons is under-studied: most agentic benchmarks are short and episodic, and performance on long tasks is hard to dissect into stored knowledge, reasoning and luck. We introduce SpireBench, in which models play the complete commercial deck-builder Slay the Spire (StS), where early decisions decide long-term success. Across 20 large language models (LLMs) at the game's highest difficulty, frontier models beat heuristic baselines and match the average human player but remain far behind experts. This gap widens as the run lengthens: the strongest models win the first act as often as experts, then fall behind. What separates strong models from weak is how well they play each fight; all of them misjudge risk over a run, preserving health rather than spending it to grow stronger. translated_title: SpireBench：利用《杀戮尖塔》评估智能体模型的长期战略博弈能力
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.12596v1 公告类型：新论文 摘要：智能体大语言模型如今已能处理复杂任务，但针对长时程的战略推理研究仍然不足：大多数智能体基准测试短小且情节化，而且模型在长任务上的表现难以分解为存储知识、推理能力和运气。我们提出SpireBench，让模型完整地游玩商业卡牌构筑游戏《杀戮尖塔》，在该游戏中早期决策决定长期成败。在最难难度下对20个大语言模型进行测试后发现：前沿模型击败了启发式基线，达到普通人类玩家的平均水平，但仍远远落后于专家玩家。这一差距随着单局进程的延长而扩大：最强的模型在第一幕的胜率与专家相当，但随后逐渐落后。区分强弱模型的关键在于它们打好每一场战斗的能力；而所有模型在整个局中都会误判风险，倾向于保留生命值而非花费生命值来换取成长。对游戏中所有术语进行全面且自洽的重命名实验表明……（摘要至此截断）
tldr: SpireBench让20个大语言模型完整游玩《杀戮尖塔》以评估长时程战略推理能力，发现前沿模型虽达到普通人类水平但远逊于专家，且随着游戏进程延长差距不断扩大，所有模型都误判长线风险，倾向保守保血而非牺牲血量换取成长。
en_tdlr: SpireBench evaluates long-horizon strategic reasoning by having 20 LLMs play the full game of Slay the Spire, revealing that frontier models match average human players but fall further behind experts as runs lengthen, and all models misjudge long-term risk by preserving health rather than spending it to grow stronger.
